subject: Post-call recap: Redwood Integration & SDK fit (next steps)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acme.com>, Tom Li <tom.li@acme.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 5 May 2027 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: Redwood Integration & SDK fit (next steps)

Hi Sarah / Tom —

Thanks for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and a proposed set of next steps so we stay aligned. Let me know if I missed anything.

Highlights / confirmed pain:
- Search relevance is inconsistent across product lines; current vector store + rerank pipeline is slow at peak (tail latencies ~800ms) and expensive.
- Need structured outputs for downstream billing and reporting (JSON with known schema).
- On-prem constraints: Tom noted strict egress policies and longer procurement lead times for dedicated hardware.
- Security: SOC 2 + key rotation and audit logs are must-haves for any pilot.

Goals we heard:
1) Improve search relevance with embeddings + lightweight reranking while keeping 95th percentile latency under 200ms for 99% of queries.
2) Ship a first integration in a sandbox environment (weeklies) and evaluate quality vs cost over a 6-week pilot.
3) Produce structured extraction for invoices and support tickets; validated JSON schema is required.

Integration / product fit notes (technical):
- SDK: We'll provide a small SDK helper to wrap streaming responses and function-calling so your engineers can get structured JSON outputs with minimal changes.
- Function calling: Use our function-call schema for the extractor. This will return validated JSON and allow deterministic downstream processing.
- Streaming: Recommended for the UI flows to keep perceived latency low; we can stream tokens + incremental JSON when using function calls.
- Embeddings + reranking: We recommend an embedding-enabled rerank step (embedding index -> top-k -> rerank with cross-encoder or lightweight transformer) to balance cost and quality.

Open items / asks from Acme:
- Estimated monthly query volume / tokens (rough range is fine) — helps us size hosted vs dedicated.
- SOC 2 evidence owner and timeline (for pilot vs production).
- Any network/firewall requirements for a sandbox (IP allowlist).

Attachments: redwood-integration-arch.png (simple flow), acme-token-estimates.xlsx (placeholder for your numbers), SOW-draft-v1.pdf (initial scope).

Next steps (proposed):
1) Sarah/Tom: share approximate monthly token/queries by EOD Wed (05/06).
2) Redwood: we’ll send a lightweight SDK example + function schema and a draft pilot plan (by Fri 05/07).
3) Schedule 30-min follow-up demo with engineering to walk through SDK usage and streaming (we suggested Thu 05/13).

If this looks right I’ll upload the SDK example to the shared Drive and open a HubSpot task under RDW-4123.

Thanks again — looking forward to the pilot.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Redwood Integration & SDK fit (next steps)

Hi all — Vivek from Redwood infra/solutions here. Quick technical follow-up and suggested pilot approach: 

1) SDK / function calling
- We’ll provide a minimal JS + Python snippet that wraps our streaming endpoint and integrates the function-call schema. The extractor function schema (example) will be a JSON schema posted to the Drive link. That lets you validate outputs on ingest.

2) Streaming + perceived latency
- For UI search flows, we recommend streaming tokens immediately and then sending a final function call response with the validated JSON. This keeps the UI responsive while ensuring downstream determinism.

3) Embeddings + rerank pattern
- Suggested pipeline:
   a) Query -> embedding -> ANN index (top 50)
   b) Lightweight reranker (cross-encoder) on top 12 results using a small transformer (we can provide a tuned checkpoint).
   c) Optionally run final function-call extractor only on top 3 to save cost.

4) Pilot infra options
- Sandbox (hosted): fastest to get started; we can enforce IP allowlist and scoped keys for your pilot.
- Dedicated / Private: given your production egress constraints, we can scope a Dedicated pool or Private deployment for later phases.

Latency/throughput expectations (estimates for pilot):
- Streaming token latency: ~8-12ms/token on our hosted endpoints for 8k context.
- End-to-end rerank (embedding lookup + reranker on top 12): ~120-220ms depending on batch sizing.

Action items from Redwood (this week):
- Share JS/Python SDK snippets + example invoice function schema (will upload to the Drive link Marissa included).
- Provide a short benchmark note for the suggested reranker checkpoint (to set expectations in your perf tests).

If you’d like, I can demo the streaming + function flow in the call on Thu 05/13.

Cheers,
Vivek
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
